# Frost Yeti

## Description
Ten feet of white fur gone stiff with rime, so that the yeti clinks when it moves and
leaves a dusting of frost on anything it brushes. Long arms, a flat blue-grey face, eyes
the pale colour of glacier ice. It smells of cold stone and old snow. When it is still, it
is a snowdrift; when it is angry, the air around it drops so fast that breath freezes in
beards. It fights like a bear that has learned patience: it waits, it watches, and then
it is suddenly very close.

## Traits
- **Ice Walk.** The yeti moves across ice and snow without difficult terrain and can't be knocked prone by slippery ground. It can climb sheer ice without a check.
- **Snow Camouflage.** The yeti has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide in snowy or icy terrain.
- **Keen Smell.** The yeti has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on smell.
- **Fear of Fire.** If the yeti takes fire damage, it has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of its next turn, and it won't willingly move closer to an open flame larger than a torch during that time.

## Attacks
| name | hit | damage | range | notes |
|------|-----|--------|-------|-------|
| claw | +6 | 1d6+4 slashing + 1d6 cold | 5 | rime-crusted claws |
| hurled ice | +6 | 2d6+4 bludgeoning | 30/60 | a block of packed snow and ice |

## Actions
- **Multiattack.** The yeti makes two claw attacks. It can replace one of them with Chilling Gaze.
- **Chilling Gaze.** One creature the yeti can see within 30 feet must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or take 7 (2d6) cold damage and have its speed halved until the end of its next turn as frost creeps up its legs. A creature immune to cold damage is unaffected.

## Reactions
(none)

## Backstory
Frost yetis are what the mountains keep instead of wolves. They live above the snow line in
pairs or alone, in caves they line with packed ice until the walls ring like bells, and they
range down to the valleys only in the worst winters, when the snow pushes the goats and
the deer below them. Mountain folk say a yeti is born from the first snowfall that nobody
heard land, which is why they hate noise: bells, shouting and drums drive them to rage or
to flight. They are clever enough to trade (a yeti will leave a goat untouched for a wheel
of cheese left on the right rock) and old enough to hold grudges across generations. They
fear fire the way other beasts fear thunder, because fire is the only thing in their world
that wins against the cold. Herders who know them pay a "snow toll"; herders who don't,
learn.
